cost: per_op O(n*closure cost), main allocation O(N*1024+64MiB), repeated shared-buffer edits copy64MiB; main intentionally not executed.
description: Timing helpers and unexecuted snapshot workload.
forward: per_op(n,f) invokes f exactly n times then divides elapsed seconds by n; fmt chooses ns if s<1e-6, microseconds if s<1e-3 else ms. Main scales1000/10000/100000 files plus64MiB and compares snapshot,restore,write,dump timings.
inverse: Formatted rounded duration admits intervals and cannot reconstruct raw clock or workload timing distribution. Per-op mean admits many individual duration sequences.
limitations: Finite checks only; partial source syntax, no expanded semantic AST.
No numerical surrogate: categorical/effect semantics lack useful metric; future caps 1/2/5/10 require domain and reference.
state: For n>0 bounded helper elapsed is finite nonnegative; timing is nondeterministic. fmt boundaries use strict less-than. n0 remains undefined useful average (infinite/NaN possible).
